claim_summary: S2S-FDD converts industrial time series into language summaries, then uses retrieved maintenance knowledge and feedback-driven sensor queries for zero-shot fault diagnosis.

claim_evidence.quote: We propose a multi-turn tree-structured diagnosis method based on LLMs. Leveraging textual time-series descriptions, the method achieves zero-shot fault diagnosis and analysis. It also supports dynamic reasoning updates based on operator feedback, forming a humanin-the-loop adaptive diagnosis loop.

modules.name: Fault-directed sensor selection and temporal summary
modules.scope_reason: The residual thresholds, fault onset, anomaly scores and candidate selection embed fault-detection criteria; if the task family changed, the detection objective and selection criterion would need redesign, so R3_1 TSK applies before temporal processing at GTS.

evidence.quote: Candidate variables are selected by top n1 anomaly scores (S1 ) and top n2 earliest fault times (S2 ), forming S = S1 ∪S2 . Final selection uses variance comparison: Sfiltered = {j ∈ S | var(Xfault [:, j]) > 2 · var(Xbase [:, j])}

modules.name: Historical fault retrieval and iterative sensor inspection
modules.scope_reason: Retrieving fault records, deciding evidence sufficiency and requesting sensor tables serves the fault diagnosis objective; changing task family would require redesigning the fault knowledge, query semantics and output, so R3_1 TSK applies before temporal context handling at GTS.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - retrieval and queries are organized around fault diagnosis

R4:Memory and Context; Tools and Execution; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: Fault records Ktarget with similarity above a threshold are included in LLM prompts to activate reasoning. Notably, a chunking operation is performed before encoding each report Kj , and after recalling a particular chunk, the corresponding full report is retrieved.

If the LLM feels that the textual information for given variables is not sufficient to infer a fault, a function calling is made to retrieve information about variables that the LLM believes may be useful for fault diagnosis.

task_performance.quote: the proposed method is effective and can achieve up to 76.92% accuracy with only 500 normal samples without any faulty sample training.

notes: Human-in-the-loop refinement is described as a capability, but the reported experiments provide accuracy evidence only; they do not evaluate expert feedback or downstream operational utility.
